title: Ring rule stays; a protocol exists only where two production adapters exist (retires P-01/P-08 'every adapter behind a port, only the container wires it')
context: P-01 (features-no-infrastructure) and P-08 (cli-no-infrastructure) required every I/O boundary to sit behind a core/protocols Protocol wired only by container.py. Measured reality (0.5.1 deepening audit, re-verified by inspection): core/protocols holds 23 Protocol classes in 22 files, 935 LOC of interface text; only 4 have two or more production adapters — TelemetryRefreshLock, FilePermissionSetter, ShutdownHandler (posix/windows pairs) and ProcessAncestry (Linux proc / ps / Windows toolhelp) — all OS-portability seams; the other 19 have exactly one infrastructure implementer and exist only to satisfy the two contracts. container.py is 880 LOC, 22 fix commits, 10 ledger records carrying 'container.py' as component, ~180 LOC of dead lifecycle closures (_definition_committer, _closure_committer, _memory_lint_gate, _repo_hygiene_sweeper, _workspace_python_bin, resolve_context) kept alive by the funnel. Ledger evidence: a grep of every 'cause'/'solution' field in specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl finds ONE mention of 'adapter' (git shallow-repo guard, fixed inside GitSubprocessClient — not a swap) and ZERO mentions of 'fake'; no bug was ever fixed by substituting an adapter behind a seam. The contracts produced the funnel they were meant to prevent: every verb needing infrastructure added a build_* function to container.py instead of a port, and 9 of the 18 capped ignore edges are exceptions to these two contracts alone (features-no-infrastructure 7, cli-no-infrastructure 2). Test fakes are not a second adapter: git_subprocess has 14 real-adapter test files and 0 fakes.
decision: We will keep the ring rule — core imports nothing internal; infrastructure imports only core; features import core and infrastructure; cli and hooks import all of them; no upward edge; features never import a sibling feature; core.kernel_tunables stays a leaf; core.specs_resolver keeps its single home — and drop the port requirement: a feature or a CLI verb imports the concrete infrastructure class it is the only consumer of, directly. A Protocol lives in core/protocols only where two or more PRODUCTION adapters exist (today: TelemetryRefreshLock, FilePermissionSetter, ShutdownHandler, ProcessAncestry); a test fake never counts as a second adapter. container.py wires only what two features share or what a platform seam selects; everything else is constructed where it is consumed. Replacement Part-1 text — P-01: 'We keep the dependency ring: core imports nothing internal, infrastructure imports only core, no layer imports upward; a feature imports the concrete infrastructure class it alone consumes.' Measured by: `lint-imports --config setup.cfg --no-cache` — contracts core-no-upper-layers and infrastructure-no-upper-layers (zero ignored imports). P-08: 'We keep a Protocol in core/protocols only where two production adapters exist; container.py composes platform seams and shared collaborators, nothing single-consumer.' Measured by: `pytest tests/contract/test_protocols_have_two_adapters.py` (AST walk: every class under core/protocols has >= 2 implementers under infrastructure/), landing in the same commit that retires the 19 single-adapter protocols.
consequences: + setup.cfg: contracts features-no-infrastructure and cli-no-infrastructure are DELETED with their 9 ignore edges; _RECORDED_IGNORE_EDGE_CAP drops 18 -> 9 and _RECORDED_CONTRACT_COUNT 9 -> 7 in the accept commit (P-10 ratchet holds: the cap only falls). The cross-feature edges (6) stay until K7; the features-no-subprocess edges (3) stay under P-02, which is untouched (one process seam, not a swap seam). + ~17 protocol files, their build_* indirections and the two-protocols-per-store pairs are deleted (~935 -> ~200 LOC of protocol text); container.py shrinks to wiring only (~250 LOC); the ~180 LOC dead closures go with it. + Tests use real adapters over tmp dirs, as git_subprocess already does; mirrored fake-based unit files are deleted per dd-test-stewardship. - A feature reaching an adapter directly cannot be substituted without editing the feature; accepted because the ledger shows zero substitutions in the project's history and four real seams remain protected. - P-01/P-08 text in ARCHITECTURE.md changes in the accept commit (`docs(adr): accept ...`), never before. Bug surface: REDUCED — the 880-LOC funnel with 22 fix commits and 10 ledger records is the only component this decision touches, and it shrinks; no ledger bug depends on the retired seams. Dependency: K9's deletion half (dead closures, single-consumer modules filed inside their feature where no contract breaks) proceeds before acceptance; protocol retirement and contract deletion wait for the operator's accept.
measured_by: lint-imports --config setup.cfg --no-cache — contracts core-no-upper-layers, infrastructure-no-upper-layers, features-no-cross-feature, kernel-tunables-is-a-leaf, bind-resolution-seam-is-a-single-home; plus pytest tests/contract/test_import_linter_ignore_cap.py re-pinned at _RECORDED_IGNORE_EDGE_CAP = 9, _RECORDED_CONTRACT_COUNT = 7

title: Git index boundary: one session per checkout is operator practice, not library code; the two shared-index bugs are deferred with that reason
context: Two open records — concurrent-sessions-share-git-index-commit-boundary-contamination (2026-08-27, `git commit --amend` swept a peer's staged histo file) and concurrent-agent-git-add-clobbers-other-sessions-staged-files-into-unrelated-commit (2026-08-27, `git add -A` swept a peer's two staged files) — have one cause: two harness sessions ran Bash in the SAME checked-out repos/<slug> tree, and git keeps exactly one index per worktree. Three options were weighed. (a) `context bind` provisions a per-session linked worktree: bind writes one session record and acquires nothing (context-management memory); a harness process cannot change its cwd after launch, so a worktree created by bind is never the tree the session commits from; gitflow allows exactly one live feature/{M.m.p} and git refuses the same branch checked out in two worktrees, so every extra worktree needs its own branch or a detached HEAD — a second branch pattern the §4 contract forbids; the open bug sdd-gate-memory-phase-resolves-empty-when-cwd-is-a-linked-worktree-outside-repos shows worktrees already break resolution (K1 fixes it); Windows adds per-worktree venv cost. Rejected. (b) pre-commit refuses when the index holds paths staged by a foreign presence: PresenceRecord carries session_id, runtime, pid, last_seen_at — no paths — so the gate would have to start recording every written path per session (new state, new reaper), git cannot attribute who ran `git add`, and the refusal blocks a human commit, violating DADAIA §3.4 (pre-commit warns and always allows) and the NO-LOCKS doctrine. A branch added to pre_commit_decision plus a new record kind is the puxadinho the standing order forbids. Rejected. (c) Nothing in the library: the index is a per-worktree resource by git's own contract; DADAIA §7.3 already states 'commit exactly what the fix touched, never a blanket -A'; the only missing statement is the operator practice.
decision: We will not add library code for the git index. The practice is: one harness session per checked-out tree; an operator who wants parallel sessions on one repo creates the linked worktree BEFORE launching the harness (`git worktree add ../<repo_slug>-<n> <branch>`) and launches it there, so each session owns its own index; every agent stages by explicit path and commits with `git commit --only <paths>` or after a path-scoped `git add`, never `-A` and never a bare `--amend` (DADAIA §7.3 already). The two records move to terminal `deferred` with reason: 'shared git index between two sessions in one checkout is a git contract, not a library contract; practice = one session per checkout/worktree; revisit only if a harness gains a per-session cwd'. Code change: 0 production LOC; owner: none — the practice belongs to the operator and to the law text (a one-line statement under DADAIA.md §3.3 'Races, mode, context', authored by ai-engineer in public/data/DADAIA.md if the operator wants it written).
consequences: + Zero new state, zero new branch, zero new reaper; pre_commit_decision stays WARN-only; presence stays path-less and advisory; bind keeps acquiring nothing; Invocation keeps one session_id. + The K1 fix for the linked-worktree resolution bug makes the practice actually work end to end (a worktree outside repos/ resolves its context). - The defect can still recur whenever an operator launches two harnesses in one tree; the pre-commit advisory WARN ('another session is live on this context') is the only signal, and it already exists. Bug surface: UNCHANGED for the library (no touched feature), and the two records leave the open set with a reason instead of a patch — the 06-10..07-22 session-model chain shows every structural fix in this area was a deletion, never an added guard.
measured_by: dadaia bugs status — both records terminal `deferred` naming this decision; pytest tests/contract/test_hooks_publication_boundary.py (pre-commit remains allow-always)

title: One Invocation: session, context, workspace, mode, release and phase are resolved once per process in core.invocation (amends P-09's single home)
context: P-09 named core.specs_resolver.resolve_context as the single home, yet eight modules re-derived context, three re-derived the session id and four re-derived staleness from the same files; 28+ ledger records, one open (sdd-gate-memory-phase-resolves-empty-when-cwd-is-a-linked-worktree-outside-repos). A single home for one fact was not enough while the neighbouring facts had many.
decision: We resolve the whole Invocation (workspace_root, session_id, context_name, repo_slug, specs_dir, mode, release, phase, rung) once per process in core.invocation.resolve and pass the value to every policy; the session record has exactly one owner in core; no module outside core.invocation reads .dadaia/sessions/ or derives a context.
consequences: + P-09 text changes its named home to core.invocation.resolve; the import-linter contract bind-resolution-seam-is-a-single-home names core.invocation and keeps zero ignore edges. + hooks build the Invocation from the payload; CLI from flags; container no longer resolves. - core.specs_resolver, core.session_env, features/spec_context/session_identity and the eight ladders are deleted. Risk: any caller that still re-derives a fact is a regression; measured by the contract test.
measured_by: lint-imports --config setup.cfg --no-cache — contract bind-resolution-seam-is-a-single-home (core.invocation, zero ignored imports); pytest tests/unit/core/test_invocation.py; grep -rn 'sessions/' dadaia_workspace --include=*.py | grep -v core/invocation returns nothing
amends: none — P-09 has ADR: none (pre-canon principle); this record is its first
